teaser: A blueprint spread across the kitchen table at midnight. A question swallowed at a parent-teacher evening instead of asked out loud. You are a 22, crossed with an INFJ's quiet reading of what a room actually needs. The 22 wants structures big enough to outlast a single lifetime; the INFJ wants those structures to feel true to the people living inside them. Here the vision does not float — it gets measured, drafted, revised at the kitchen table more than once. What is particular to this crossing is the weight: feeling responsible for the shape of something enormous, while still noticing who got left out of the plan.
excerpt: Three times tonight you have rehearsed the sentence that explains why the project matters more than the dinner reservation.
